sections.title: Official rule
sections.body: The official LSE Master of Public Policy page states that applicants must have at least five years of policy-relevant experience, although exceptions may be granted for outstanding candidates with slightly less experience. It also describes the programme as designed for mid-career professionals with more than five years’ experience. Therefore, five years is a formal stated admissions expectation with a discretionary exception—not simply a preference used only to rank otherwise eligible applicants.

sections.title: Applicant’s roles
sections.body: The authorised employment history records policy analyst work at the Accra Metropolitan Research Unit from September 5, 2022 to December 15, 2023, and research assistant work at the Institute for Fiscal Studies from March 4, 2024 to the present. On August 8, 2026, these periods total approximately 3 years 8 months, excluding the documented December 16, 2023–March 3, 2024 transition gap. Both roles appear substantively policy-relevant based on the CV’s description of municipal revenue, social-protection targeting, and quasi-experimental evaluation work.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: The roles can plausibly be presented as relevant professional policy experience, but they do not satisfy the ordinary five-year threshold. Lena would need to rely on LSE’s stated exception for an outstanding candidate with slightly less experience. Her First Class BA, 3.78/4.00 GPA, strong quantitative coursework, Dean’s Award, and applied policy research record are potentially relevant strengths, but the official source does not guarantee that these facts will secure an exception. The appropriate classification is: standard experience expectation not met; possible discretionary exception; not an automatic eligibility pass.

follow_ups: If applying, explicitly explain the policy impact and quantitative content of both roles and ask LSE SPP whether approximately 3 years 8 months would be considered within its 'slightly less experience' exception.
